text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-severity: SEA1 serving pools reporting 100% pod eviction and control-plane heartbeat loss. auto-escalation triggered.
alyssa: seeing increased 503s from customers in APAC, confirmed elevated error budget. Dashboards show API latency spike at 03:12 UTC. :eyes:
marco: copying logs — control-plane API master stream shows repeated 'etcd: request timed out' and kubelet disconnects.
kyra: ran quick health check: `./tools/region-health --region=sea1 --summary` output: `nodes: 0 ready / 48 total, pods crashing, network flaps detected`.
alyssa: rolling: are we dealing with a network fabric issue or underlying host eviction? any provider alerts?
devops: provider status page (asia-southeast-1) shows "degraded networking" starting ~03:05 UTC. I've opened a ticket with the cloud provider (#INC-4621).
marco: plan: 1) stop new deployments to SEA1 2) shift production traffic off SEA1 to SFO1 + IAD2 3) gate inbound ingress and fail traffic gradually to preserve sessions.
ops-runbook: recommended cutover play (short):
```
- disable new LB sessions to SEA1: `rbacctl set-backend-probability sea1 0`
- update route policy: `traffic-router promote sfo1,iad2 for region=apac priority=1`
- enable read-only fallback for long lived sessions
```
oncall: I'll be incident lead for now. Marco/DevOps please confirm when you start the cutover. I will coordinate comms and paging. :white_check_mark:
marco: starting step 1 now — pausing autoscaler jobs and blocking new deploy webhooks. Exec: `kubectl scale deployment autoscaler --replicas=0 -n infra`
kyra: quick check of KV cache showed heavy evictions, likely due to network partition + disk IO on control-plane nodes. snapshot: `KV_CACHE_HIT=1.2%`
devops: traffic-router change in progress, directing 60% -> sfo1, 40% -> iad2 as a warm handoff. monitoring for error surge.
alyssa: noticed a spike in token generation latency for streaming endpoints, setting a rate limit at the edge to reduce token pressure.
marco: logs show a flapping mTLS handshake failure between the control-plane and node manager: `tls: handshake failure: EOF` — might be provider network ACL.
ops-runbook: escalation tip: if provider can't confirm within 15m, prepare for extended outage play and escalate to account team for capacity reservations in alternative regions.
oncall: agreed. Notifying CS and status page. Please post short updates here every 5 minutes.
alyssa: posted interim status on status.redwood.ai and customer-facing Slack channel.
devops: provider replied: investigating fabric issue, estimated mitigation 30-45m. They suggest instance-level reboots as temporary mitigation; holding until we finish traffic shift.
marco: traffic shift at 03:22 UTC completed to warm handoff percentages. Observability: 503s dropped from 18%->6%, CPU in sfo1 rising but healthy.
kyra: continuing checks on KV consistency and ongoing pod restarts. If we hit >10% errors again, we'll enact full evacuation and scale up dedicated pools in SFO1.
oncall: good progress. Keeping this channel for ops-only. Update in 5.
